name.text: WAT 18.1: Functions Are Values Here Too!

questiontext.text:
Goal

A bottling line sends every bottle through a sequence of processing stations. One station can replace another when both accept and return the same kind of bottle. A station switched off for the shift remains in the sequence.

Read
  • Function types. Read the first sentence, the rule about parameter names, and the final examples. How do you write a function type that accepts an int and returns an int?
  • Read the second sentence of the same section. What does an unassigned Step variable hold?
  • Function literals. Read the first sentence and its example. How do you write an unnamed function where a value is expected? What type does it have?
Coming from Java

The reflex is a functional interface plus a lambda or method reference that the compiler converts at the call site.

@FunctionalInterface
interface Step { int apply(int n); }

int applyAll(int x, Step... steps) { ... }
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • If the compiler rejects double as a Step, compare your declaration with the section's list of example types.
  • If a hidden test panics, reread the second sentence of Function types and ask what an unassigned Step holds.

testcode.text: fmt.Println(applyAll(1, double), applyAll(-3, double, double, double))
fmt.Println(applyAll(3, double, func(n int) int { return n + 1 }))
var off Step fmt.Println(applyAll(4, double, off, double)) fmt.Println(applyAll(5))

questiontext.text:
Goal

A chess leaderboard lists the highest score first and sorts tied players by name. Post the board after both the four-player semi-final and the thirteen-player final.

Read
  • sort.Slice. Read the signature and the sentence that links to the Interface type's Less method. What do i and j index? Which values does less not receive directly?
  • Find the sentence about stability. What can happen to two players with the same score?
Coming from Java

The reflex is a Comparator, or a sort by name followed by a sort by score. The second route trusts the name order to survive the score sort.

players.sort(comparing(Player::name));
players.sort(comparing(Player::score).reversed());
Required: sort.Slice
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • Your less receives two index positions, so reach the players through the slice rank was given.
  • If the visible tests pass and a hidden one fails, reread the sentence on equal elements.

expected.text: Cy 30 Fay 30 Ivy 30 Lee 30 Bo 20 Ed 20 Hal 20 Kim 20 Ada 10 Di 10 Gus 10 Jo 10 Max 10
Ada 30 Cy 30 Ed 30 Gus 30 Ivy 30 Kim 30 Max 30 Bo 20 Di 20 Fay 20 Hal 20 Jo 20 Lee 20 0

name.text: WAT 18.3: The Ticket Machine That Remembers!

questiontext.text:
Goal

A fairground ticket machine issues tickets in number order. It has no storage drawer for the current number. The fair uses several machines, and each gate admits a fixed number of visitors before locking.

Read
  • Function closures. Read both paragraphs. What can the returned function do to a variable declared outside its body? What does each closure bind to?
  • Run the example. Why do pos and neg print different values on the same line?
Coming from Java

The reflex is a class with a private int field and a next() method. Java keeps the count in the field because a lambda may only read what it captured.

class TicketMachine {
    private int count;
    int next() { return ++count; }
}
Banned: struct, type
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • Add a third adder to the page's example and see whether its first result carries on from the other two.
  • If two machines count 1, 2, 3, 4 between them, compare where you declared the count with where the example declares sum.

testcode.text: a, b := newMachine(), newMachine() fmt.Println(a(), a(), b(), a(), b()) fmt.Println(a(), b())

expected.text: ticket 1 ticket 2 ticket 3 locked locked false true
